subject: Agriculture
title: Organic Matter
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Organic Matter.

hook.text: Organic matter makes up only 5% of most soils—but it drives almost everything that matters.

buildup.text: Dead leaves, roots, insect bodies, and manure all decompose into a dark substance called humus.

discovery.text: Humus holds water like a sponge—up to six times its weight—and slowly releases nutrients to plant roots.

twist.text: Tilling soil exposes organic matter to air, speeding decomposition. Intensive farming burns through humus fast.

climax.text: Rebuilding organic matter takes years of cover cropping and compost. Losing it takes one bad season.

punchline.text: Five percent of the soil does fifty percent of the work.

quiz.question: What is humus?
options: Decomposed organic matter that holds water and nutrients in soil
